excerpt: EdgeOne Makers is Tencent's platform for deploying web apps and AI agents on its edge network, with a permanent free plan. Plans, features and alternatives.
content:
EdgeOne Makers is Tencent Cloud's platform for shipping web apps and AI agents on the EdgeOne edge network. You connect a GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket repository (or use the CLI), set the build command and output folder, and it deploys globally with custom domains and automatic SSL. It supports full-stack frameworks such as Next.js and Nuxt, static site generators such as Astro and Hexo, and React and Vue apps, with serverless functions and storage.

For AI agents, Makers adds a built-in runtime, a sandbox for tools, conversational memory, a model gateway and observability, and works with agent frameworks such as LangGraph and the OpenAI Agents SDK. Tencent's launch post on X says web apps and agents can live in the same project, sharing deployment, monitoring and domains. Makers grew out of EdgeOne Pages and sits inside Tencent EdgeOne, which also sells CDN, DNS, WAF, DDoS protection and bot management.

Tencent announced on X that Makers went live on 23 June 2026. EdgeOne's site says the Free plan is permanent and needs no credit card; paid EdgeOne plans run from $57 a month for Basic to $590 for Standard, with a lower-priced Personal plan.

Tencent EdgeOne launched on Product Hunt on 24 June 2026 and finished #1 for the day, with 613 upvotes and 163 comments (as of 14 October 2026).

We have not tested EdgeOne Makers ourselves. This page brings together EdgeOne's official product and pricing pages, Tencent's own posts on X, its Product Hunt listing and the official pricing pages of comparable platforms, and says where each fact comes from.

profile.category: Developer tools / web and AI agent hosting
profile.starts_at: Free plan; paid EdgeOne plans from $1.4/month
profile.summary_short: Tencent's edge platform for deploying web apps and AI agents from Git or the CLI
use_cases: Deploying a Next.js, Nuxt, Astro or React site from Git with automatic SSL
Hosting an AI agent with sandboxed tools, memory and tracing without running your own servers
Adding an agent to an existing web project and serving both from one domain
Serving sites to users in Asia, where EdgeOne lists 2,500+ of its 3,200+ nodes

fit: developers who want Vercel-style Git deploys plus hosted agent infrastructure in one place
teams with users in Asia or mainland China who want an edge network strong in that region
hobbyists who want a permanent free tier with no credit card
not_fit: anyone who needs Makers-specific pricing spelled out up front: the pricing page lists EdgeOne plans, not Makers usage limits
teams that must keep data with a non-Chinese cloud provider for policy reasons
people who only need a static page and already use another free host

pricing.intro: Makers runs on Tencent EdgeOne's plans. The pricing page lists the EdgeOne plans below with a "$" sign; it does not give separate Makers prices, and Edge Functions show "overuse payment" on paid plans.

plans.name: Free
plans.detail: No credit card. CDN, platform DDoS protection, basic access control, WAF ruleset, basic CC protection, free SSL; edge function requests listed as unmetered

plans.name: Personal
plans.detail: 50 GB traffic, 3M requests, 1 site, 200 sub-domains, 20 rules

plans.name: Basic
plans.detail: 500 GB traffic, 20M requests, 1 site, 300 sub-domains, 50 rules

plans.name: Standard
plans.detail: 3 TB traffic, 50M requests, OWASP Top 10 managed rules, bot management

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.detail: On-demand traffic and requests, 10 sites, dedicated DDoS protection

notes: Usage above a plan's quota is billed hourly, per the pricing FAQ.
Add-ons such as Smart Acceleration, QUIC and Bot Management are $0.0143 per VAU (100 VAU per 1M requests).

alternatives.intro: Other platforms for deploying web apps and serverless code. Prices come from each product's own pricing page, checked on 14 October 2026.

items.name: Vercel
items.what: Frontend and full-stack hosting from the makers of Next.js
items.difference: The reference platform for Next.js; agent hosting relies on its functions and AI SDK rather than a built-in agent sandbox and memory.

items.name: Netlify
items.what: Git-based hosting for web apps with serverless and edge functions
items.difference: Long-established Git deploy workflow; no built-in agent runtime of the kind Makers advertises.

items.name: Cloudflare Workers and Pages
items.what: Serverless code and site hosting on Cloudflare's global network
items.starts_at: Free tier; see its pricing page
items.difference: The closest like-for-like option: serverless code, sites, CDN and security on one global network, from a different provider.

pros: Permanent free plan with no credit card
Web apps and AI agents deploy together from Git or the CLI
Built-in agent sandbox, memory, model gateway and observability
Large edge network, especially in Asia
cons: No separate published pricing or limits for Makers itself
The Personal plan price is shown as two figures without explanation
Overage is billed hourly, so costs can be harder to predict
No public contact email; support goes through a contact form and community channels

posts.text: Tencent EdgeOne introduces EdgeOne Makers, the edge platform to build and deploy web apps and agents through CLI, Skills, IDE plugins, Git and CI/CD.
posts.author: Tencent EdgeOne

posts.text: Tencent EdgeOne announces that Makers is going live on 23 June 2026.
posts.author: Tencent EdgeOne

faq.a: Tencent Cloud's platform for deploying web apps and AI agents on the EdgeOne edge network, from Git or the CLI, with functions, storage and built-in agent infrastructure.
There is a Free plan that EdgeOne says is permanent and needs no credit card. Paid EdgeOne plans are Personal, Basic ($57 a month), Standard ($590 a month) and Enterprise.
Next.js, Nuxt, Astro, Hexo, React and Vue for web apps, and agent frameworks such as LangGraph and the OpenAI Agents SDK.

faq.q: How is it different from EdgeOne Pages?
faq.a: Makers grew out of EdgeOne Pages: it keeps the web hosting, functions and storage and adds an agent runtime with sandbox, memory, model gateway and observability.

faq.q: What happens if I go over my plan's quota?
faq.a: EdgeOne's pricing FAQ says usage above the quota is billed in hourly billing cycles.

faq.q: What are the alternatives to EdgeOne Makers?
faq.a: Vercel, Netlify and Cloudflare Workers and Pages are the closest like-for-like platforms.
